{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_80","type":"agent_message","text":"Here is the exact circular dependency!\n```\n┌──->──┐\n|  springLoggingAutoConfiguration (field java.util.Optional pl.piomin.logging.config.SpringLoggingAutoConfiguration.template)\n└──<-──┘\n```\n\nLet's understand why this happens.\n`SpringLoggingAutoConfiguration` has:\n```java\n\t@Autowired(required = false)\n\tOptional<RestTemplate> template;\n```\nWhen Spring is preparing dependencies for the `springLoggingAutoConfiguration` bean (before it is even instantiated fully/initialized), it sees it needs an `Optional<RestTemplate>`.\nTo resolve `Optional<RestTemplate>`, Spring scans all bean definitions of type `RestTemplate`. It finds the bean definition `restTemplate()` defined in `SpringLoggingAutoConfiguration` itself!\nBecause the bean definition `restTemplate()` is defined in `SpringLoggingAutoConfiguration` as a non-static factory method, Spring realizes it needs an instance of `springLoggingAutoConfiguration` to invoke the `restTemplate()` method.\nWait! This forms a direct cycle during bean creation:\n`springLoggingAutoConfiguration` bean creation requires `template` autowiring.\nTo resolve `template` autowiring, Spring needs to evaluate or instantiate all `RestTemplate` beans.\nTo instantiate the `restTemplate` bean definition, Spring needs `springLoggingAutoConfiguration` bean instance to invoke the factory method on.\nBoom! `BeanCurrentlyInCreationException`.\n\nWhy didn't this happen in Spring Boot 2.1?\nBecause in older Spring versions, maybe Spring didn't try to greedily resolve and build the bean of type `Optional<RestTemplate>` first, or maybe it broke circular references because of circular reference resolution on factory method beans being treated differently, or because `@ConditionalOnMissingBean` behaves slightly differently under newer Spring, or because circular references were allowed.\nActually, in Spring Boot 2.6+, circular references are explicitly prohibited by default, but even with circular references permitted, this particular dynamic (non-static `@Bean` method resolving onto the very config class field being autowired) can fail during context boot depending on bean creation order.\n\nHow should we fix this clean and elegant?\nWait!\nIf `restTemplate()` is made a **static** bean method, then Spring does NOT need an instance of `SpringLoggingAutoConfiguration` to invoke the `restTemplate()` method!\nLet's think: is that true?\nYes! A static `@Bean` method does not require an instance of the declaring `@Configuration` class to be created first!\nWait, but does the static method reference any instances or fields of `SpringLoggingAutoConfiguration`?\nLet's see:\n```java\n\t@Bean\n\t@ConditionalOnMissingBean(RestTemplate.class)\n\tpublic static RestTemplate restTemplate() {\n\t\tRestTemplate restTemplate = new RestTemplate();\n\t\tList<ClientHttpRequestInterceptor> interceptorList = new ArrayList<ClientHttpRequestInterceptor>();\n\t\tinterceptorList.add(new RestTemplateSetHeaderInterceptor());\n\t\trestTemplate.setInterceptors(interceptorList);\n\t\treturn restTemplate;\n\t}\n```\nWait, the method does NOT access `this` or any instance/field of `SpringLoggingAutoConfiguration`! It only creates `RestTemplate`, registers `RestTemplateSetHeaderInterceptor`, and returns it.\nSo making `restTemplate()` **static** is extremely clean and avoids needing `SpringLoggingAutoConfiguration` instanced first.\nWait, but wait! Does that completely solve the circular dependency on `Optional<RestTemplate>`?\nLet's trace:\nIf `restTemplate()` is static, then Spring doesn't need to instantiate `SpringLoggingAutoConfiguration` to instantiate `restTemplate`.\nSo, to resolve `Optional<RestTemplate>` field dependency on `SpringLoggingAutoConfiguration`:\nSpring can instantiate `restTemplate` bean first (by calling the static method, without instantiating `SpringLoggingAutoConfiguration`), then instantiate `SpringLoggingAutoConfiguration`, inject the `restTemplate` bean into `template` field, done! No cycle!\nWait, this is incredibly elegant. Let's see if there is another way too.\nWhat if we also use `@Lazy` or change how we configure the existing templates?\nIf we use a separate `@Configuration` class, or static inner configuration class, is that even better?\nYes, Spring often suggests:\n\"If a bean is needed in a configuration class, either inject it on the method where it is needed, or move the bean definition to a separate configuration class.\"\nWait! Let's look at how the `template` is used in `SpringLoggingAutoConfiguration`:\n```java\n\t@Autowired(required = false)\n\tOptional<RestTemplate> template;\n\n    // ...\n\n\t@PostConstruct\n\tpublic void init() {\n\t\ttemplate.ifPresent(restTemplate -> {\n\t\t\tList<ClientHttpRequestInterceptor> interceptorList = new ArrayList<ClientHttpRequestInterceptor>();\n\t\t\tinterceptorList.add(new RestTemplateSetHeaderInterceptor());\n\t\t\trestTemplate.setInterceptors(interceptorList);\n\t\t});\n\t}\n```\nWait! It iterates through `template` (which has a single `RestTemplate` if any exists) or is there another pattern?\nWhy is there `@PostConstruct`?\nIf some other configuration defines a `RestTemplate` (and thus `restTemplate()` bean here is *not* created because of `@ConditionalOnMissingBean(RestTemplate.class)`), then `template` will hold that other `RestTemplate`.\nThen, in `@PostConstruct init()`, we add our `RestTemplateSetHeaderInterceptor` to it!\nWait!
